Share Price Down, Profit Outlook Up: The Company Behind Zoff

Intermestic (262A, Tokyo Stock Exchange), the operator of the Japanese budget eyewear brand Zoff, has seen its share price fall about 36% over the past year (1,662 yen as of October 2). As of October 6, quotes appear in the mid-1,690 yen range depending on the site. Figures differ slightly by source, so we recommend checking the exact closing price on your brokerage screen. Yet the earnings trend is moving in the opposite direction from the share price. This gap is the most interesting point about the stock right now.

What Kind of Company Is It?

  • It is an SPA company (a model in which one company handles everything from planning to sales) that designs, manufactures and sells eyeglass lenses, frames and sunglasses.
  • In Japan it handles the entire process from planning to sales, while overseas it acts as a franchise headquarters. Overseas entities run retail as franchisees, mainly opening stores in Asia.
  • It also sells accessories such as eyeglass and contact lens cases and cleaners.

Earnings: High Progress at the Interim Stage

In the interim results announced on August 7, ordinary profit was about 4.7 billion yen, reported as roughly 66% of the company's full-year forecast (about 7.1 billion yen). Some sources put the full-year forecast at about 11.5% revenue growth and about 24.6% ordinary profit growth. Having reached nearly two-thirds of the annual target in half a year suggests room to hit it, but eyewear retail has seasonal variation, so the second half still needs to be watched. The next earnings release is known to be scheduled for November 10.

PER (price-to-earnings ratio) shows how many times earnings per share the stock price is. A lower figure means the stock is cheaper relative to profit, but growth and industry conditions must be considered too. The share price is also more than 10% below its mid-August level, which could be read as a cool market reaction after the earnings release, but the reason is unconfirmed and remains speculation.

Shareholders: Very Large Major Holders

  • KK Rui Bosuton: 34.91%
  • Ueno (Hiroshi): 10.69%
  • Ueno (Tsuyoshi): 8.20%
  • Goldman Sachs International: 6.54%
  • Sumitomo Mitsui DS Asset Management: 4.98%

The top five shareholders alone exceed 60%. Stable major holdings are an advantage, but the shares actually traded in the market (free float) may be small, so the price can swing sharply depending on supply and demand. Between September 20 and October 1, the only change was KK Rui Bosuton's stake edging from 34.92% to 34.91%. It is not a holding of Korea's National Pension Service.

Checkpoints

  • Whether the November 10 earnings show the full-year forecast is on track, and the possibility of an upward revision
  • How quickly the overseas franchise business (Asian store openings) contributes to profit
  • Whether the share price drop is a temporary correction or reflects structural concerns in the market
  • The yen exchange rate, Japanese consumer trends and cost pressures
